recommendation: Keep the audit commit. If a future rendered build still fails to visually distinguish interfaces from abstract classes in a particular generated view, handle that as publisher/rendering follow-up rather than a core source semantic correction for FHIR-31964.
issue_request: FHIR-31964 was Published / Persuasive with Modification for R5. It reported generated ElementDefinition.path values for CanonicalResource fields on resources such as CapabilityStatement.copyright and requested clearer differentiation between CanonicalResource as an interface, DomainResource as an abstract class, and rendered inheritance/interface indicators.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-31964 was found. The current active source already defines CanonicalResource as an interface in fhir.ini and in its StructureDefinition, while CapabilityStatement, ValueSet, and StructureDefinition are active build resources that redeclare CanonicalResource fields with resource-local paths.
additional_context: The Jira comment says CanonicalResource is an interface, not a class, and not all canonical resources expose all canonical elements the same way. Current UML and StructureDefinition documentation explains that implementing classes redeclare interface attributes and associations. Related FHIR-37791 has already been reconciled on the combined branch and further clarifies interface behavior.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current FHIR source already conveys the intended interface semantics, and changing CapabilityStatement.copyright to CanonicalResource.copyright would contradict the documented redeclaration model.

related_jiras.note: Clarified interface behavior for StructureDefinition.context, SearchParameter.base, Reference.type, ElementDefinition.type.*, and interface constraints; already represented on the combined branch.
